uncertain.title: Species Detail / Named Birds map pins (DOM markers) have no keyboard access path
uncertain.description: The shared SightingsMap renders each sighting pin as a react-map-gl <Marker> whose content is a plain <div> with a click handler routed through Marker onClick — no tabIndex, no role, no keydown handler — so a keyboard user can never open the per-coordinate popup. On Species Detail ("Sighting Locations" map) that popup is the ONLY place exposing the per-sighting checklist links for sightings without comments (Top Locations rows at SpeciesDetail.tsx:1122-1137 show only name+count; the Comments section only covers commented sightings), so those eBird links are pointer-only functionality. Same pattern, lower impact (keyboard equivalents exist nearby): TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 chip markers (mitigated by the sidebar "Nearest Targets" locate buttons opening the same popup) and BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 geographic-stats rank pins (popup content fully duplicated in the adjacent "Top locations" text lists). Named Birds card maps are also unreachable but each row already lists every sighting's checklist link (NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100). Note ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim covers only the Map Explorer GL markers; these DOM-marker maps have no equivalent of its in-view lists.
uncertain.fix: DOM markers CAN be focusable (unlike the GL pins): make the marker content a <button aria-label={locName + ' — N sightings'}> so Tab+Enter opens the popup, or reuse the Map Explorer pattern (a focusable list of coordinates that drives the same selectedCoord state). For Species Detail specifically, alternatively surface the per-coordinate checklist links in the keyboard-reachable Top Locations rows.

uncertain.title: Settings tab reorder is drag-and-drop only — no keyboard alternative
uncertain.description: Tab Layout rows are reordered exclusively via HTML5 drag-and-drop on the <li draggable> (onDragStart/onDragOver/onDrop, Settings.tsx:712-717). The drag handle is a non-focusable <div aria-label="Drag to reorder…"> (line 721-723) — it isn't even in the tab order, and there are no move-up/move-down buttons. The component self-documents the failure with an sr-only note at line 699 ("Keyboard reordering is not supported in this version"), which is honest disclosure but still a WCAG 2.1.1 failure: the reorder function is entirely unavailable to keyboard (and screen-reader) users. The per-row show/hide eye toggles ARE proper buttons, so only ordering is blocked.
uncertain.fix: Add visible Move up / Move down buttons per row (simplest, also helps touch+AT), or implement the APG keyboard drag pattern (focusable handle, Space to grab, arrows to move, Space to drop, with an aria-live announcement). Then delete the sr-only disclaimer.

uncertain.title: Mobile filter sidebar: Escape focus-restore is dead code, trap snapshot goes stale, other close paths drop focus — published a11y claim is false
uncertain.wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (and 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap A integrity)
uncertain.description: Three defects in the one focus trap the app ships: (1) The Escape handler runs `setSidebarOpen(false); filtersButtonRef.current?.focus()` (lines 200-203), but the Filters button is inside the FAB cluster rendered only when the sidebar is CLOSED (`{!sidebarOpen && (<div className="sr-map-fab-cluster">` at line 1446, ref at 1461). While the sidebar is open the ref is null, so the restore is a no-op; the focused element then gets display:none (`.sr-map-sidebar-hidden`) and the browser dumps focus to <body> — the keyboard user restarts from the top of the document. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 51 explicitly claims 'Escape closes it and returns focus to the button that opened it' — that claim is currently false. (2) The focusable list is snapshotted once at open (lines 192-196: `sidebar.querySelectorAll(...)`, then `first`/`last` captured); the sidebar contains a Filters accordion and async-loaded hotspot/target lists, so after content changes Tab escapes the trap into obscured background content (the page behind is not inert). (3) The mobile 'Close filters' button (line 1414) and the backdrop click (line 1400) close via `setSidebarOpen(false)` with no focus restore — same display:none → body drop.
uncertain.fix: Keep the FAB cluster mounted while the sidebar is open (hide it with CSS/inert) so the ref survives, or restore focus in an effect that runs after sidebarOpen flips to false. Re-query focusables on each Tab keydown (HelpDocs.tsx:258-273 already does this correctly — reuse that pattern). Route ALL close paths (Escape, Close button, backdrop) through one close() that restores focus.

uncertain.title: Selected state not programmatically exposed on segmented controls and toggle pills
uncertain.description: The shared SegControl renders plain <button>s whose active option is conveyed only by background/border/font-weight — no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radiogroup semantics. It is used for the Map Explorer radius (MapExplorer.tsx:700), breeding filter (:881), Pins/Heatmap display mode (:912), and All/Week (:1285). uncertain.title: Media Targets keyboard path is partial and ACCESSIBILITY.md overstates it
uncertain.description: Media Target chips are DOM <Marker>s with a click-only <div> (no tabindex/role), so the chips themselves are not operable by keyboard. The only keyboard route to a target popup is the 'Nearest Targets' list (MapExplorer.tsx:1292-1338), which is hard-capped at 10 items sorted by distance from the SEARCH CENTER (nearest10 useMemo, MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) — it is not scoped to the map viewport, does not update on pan/zoom, and shows no over-cap hint. Any target beyond the nearest 10 (easy with a 25-50 mi radius) has no keyboard path at all. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 claims "The Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list works the same way" and that "These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom" — that is true for sightings/hotspots (cap 200, BoundsTracker-driven) but false for targets, so the published statement is currently inaccurate.
uncertain.fix: Render an InViewMarkerList for targets like the other two modes (items = locationGroups filtered by mapBounds via markersInView, cap 200 with the over-cap hint), keeping 'Nearest Targets' as a convenience list; or at minimum correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center, not viewport-scoped.

uncertain.title: Help overlay: fixed 200px TOC sidebar never collapses — content column collapses to ~30px at 320px width
uncertain.description: The HelpDocs body lays the TOC and content side by side with inline styles only — no media query and no wrap. The TOC is `width: 200, flexShrink: 0`, the row adds `padding: '0 24px'` and `gap: 40`, so at a 320 CSS px viewport (e.g. 1280px window at 400% zoom, or a phone) the help content column gets roughly 320 − 48 − 200 − 40 ≈ 32px. Markdown text wraps at one or two characters per line (long words overflow), making the in-app documentation effectively unreadable exactly for the low-vision users most likely to need it. Every other layout in the app handles this (globals.css has a 640px media query; TabNav measures and collapses), so this is the one true reflow failure found. It also contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 ("The layout reflows for narrow windows and at large sizes … without clipping content").
uncertain.fix: Below a narrow-width breakpoint (~700px), stack the TOC above the content (flexDirection column) or move it behind a disclosure button. A `.sr-help-body` class plus a rule in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css is the smallest change; alternatively reuse the TabNav measurement pattern.

uncertain.title: Contrast claim is overstated: informational text rendered in the --sr-text-disabled token sits at 2.3–2.6:1 in both themes
uncertain.description: ACCESSIBILITY.md claims body text and primary interface text meet 4.5:1 in both themes, with exactly one disclosed exception (percentage labels inside chart bars). In fact, real informational text — not disabled controls — is rendered in --sr-text-disabled, which computes to 2.56:1 light (#A1A1AA on #FFFFFF) / 2.45:1 on the page bg, and 2.29:1 dark (#52525B on #18181B). Locations: Checklists.tsx:177 and :668 (the result-count labels that are also the polite live regions), MediaCommentsSection.tsx:100 and NamedBirdsTable.tsx:77 (count labels), SpeciesDetail.tsx:461 ('{n} species' count) and :584 (scientific names inside the species-combobox options), ChecklistComparer.tsx:534 (italic placeholder labels), and the uppercase mini-headers in SetupRequired.tsx:56, ListComparer.tsx:203, HelpDocs.tsx:354. None of these are covered by the statement's disclosed chart-label exception, so the published claim is false as written, and low-vision users genuinely cannot read these labels.
uncertain.fix: Use --sr-text-muted (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark — already passing) for all informational text and reserve --sr-text-disabled strictly for genuinely disabled controls; or add a passing 'faint text' token. Then re-verify the ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast paragraph.

uncertain.title: Breeding-code badge contrast fails — in the exact category ACCESSIBILITY.md cites as exemplary (down to 1.71:1 in dark theme)
uncertain.description: The statement says interface colors meet AA, 'for example, the top breeding-code badge uses dark text on its light tier color.' That is true only for the Breeding Codes table's tier-1 badge (BreedingCodeTable.tsx:219, #3B0764 on #C084FC = 5.68:1 light / 7.31:1 dark). Elsewhere the same badge concept fails: (1) ChecklistComparer's BreedingBadge uses `color: var(--sr-on-accent)` on `background: TIER_COLORS[def.tier]` — light theme: white on tier-1 #C084FC = 2.64:1; dark theme: #052E16 on tier-2 #A855F7 = 3.77:1, tier-3 #7C3AED = 2.62:1, tier-4 #6B21A8 = 1.71:1 (the badge text is essentially illegible in dark mode). (2) BreedingCodeTable.tsx:218-219 badge in dark theme: white on tier-2 #A855F7 = 3.96:1 (0.6875rem bold = small text, needs 4.5). (3) SpeciesDetail.tsx:788 breeding pill renders its label in TIER_COLORS[tier]; for tier 1 in light theme that is #C084FC on a near-white 8%-tinted surface ≈ 2.6:1. The published example claim is materially false outside the one table.
uncertain.fix: In ChecklistComparer, reuse the BreedingCodeTable pattern: per-tier text color (`--sr-tier-1-text` on tier 1, white on tiers 3-4) instead of --sr-on-accent, and add a dark-theme tier-2 text token (white on #A855F7 fails; #1A0030-style dark text passes at ~4.97:1); for the SpeciesDetail pill, use the darker tier-text token rather than the raw tier color for tier 1.

uncertain.title: axe color-contrast: 139 runtime instances in light theme, traceable to ~4 token-level causes
uncertain.description: axe-core rule `color-contrast` (impact: serious), 139 violating nodes across all 10 tabs at default (light) theme, deduped by failing color pair: (a) --sr-accent #2D8653 (globals.css:29) used as small text fails by a hair on every light surface — 4.32:1 on #f9fafb (active tab label in TabNav, all 10 tabs), 4.03:1 on #e8f5ee accent-bg (selected segmented/sort buttons, 24x), 4.11–4.33:1 on #f4f4f5/#fafafa (links, 9x); (b) --sr-text-muted #71717A (globals.css:18) on --sr-surface-subtle #f4f4f5 = 4.39:1 — the 66 "Jump to section" nav pills (BirdingStats.tsx:450) and similar chips; (c) --sr-text-disabled #A1A1AA (globals.css:19) used for INFORMATIVE text at 2.33–2.56:1 — result-count announcements ("87 comments" aria-live spans in Checklists/LifeList), empty date-input text (color: var(--sr-text-disabled) at SpeciesDetail.tsx:638 etc.), "267 species" counts — worst offenders; (d) chart/inline labels: hardcoded white 10px % labels on --sr-graph-photo #3B82F6 bars = 3.67:1 (BirdingStats.tsx:1153, 5x) and on --sr-graph-video #8B5CF6 = 4.23:1; --sr-tier-1 #C084FC 1.5rem-bold breeding "Possible" count on white = 2.64:1, below even the 3:1 large-text threshold (BirdingStats.tsx:1613); --sr-accent-border-strong text "Loaded from Settings" on accent-bg = 2.52:1 (ListComparer); Settings date-format sublabels 3.16–3.33:1.
uncertain.fix: Token-level fixes in globals.css :root — darken --sr-accent to ~#277448 (≥4.5 on #f4f4f5) and --sr-text-muted to ~#65656e; stop using --sr-text-disabled for informative text (counts, date values) — switch those to --sr-text-muted; for chart labels either darken the bar fills the white text sits on or move labels outside the bars; use --sr-tier-1 only for swatches, not text, or pair the tier-1 stat with a darker text token.

uncertain.title: axe aria-prohibited-attr: aria-label on non-interactive drag-handle <div>s in Tab Layout settings
uncertain.description: axe-core rule `aria-prohibited-attr` (impact: serious), 9 instances (one per tab row) on the Settings tab. aria-label is prohibited on an element with an implicit generic role, so the "Drag to reorder X tab" name is ignored or inconsistently exposed by AT — and since the handle is a plain div, it is not focusable or operable by keyboard anyway (the sr-only caveat note at Settings.tsx:699 acknowledges mouse-only reorder).
uncertain.fix: Short term: drop the aria-label (or change the div to aria-hidden="true") so the prohibited attribute is gone and the handle is honestly decorative. Proper fix: make the handle a <button> with that aria-label plus keyboard reorder (ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the row), which would also retire the mouse-only caveat.

uncertain.title: axe aria-hidden-focus: focusable recharts SVG inside aria-hidden observer-pie wrapper
uncertain.wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 2.4.3 Focus Order A)
uncertain.description: axe-core rule `aria-hidden-focus` (impact: serious), 1 instance on the Statistics tab. The decorative observers donut is wrapped in <div aria-hidden="true">, but the recharts <PieChart> renders its SVG with tabIndex=0 (recharts accessibilityLayer default), so keyboard users Tab into an element that screen readers cannot perceive — a focus ghost with no announcement.
uncertain.fix: Pass accessibilityLayer={false} (or tabIndex={-1}) to this PieChart so the hidden decorative chart is also removed from the tab order. Audit the other aria-hidden chart wrappers for the same recharts default.

uncertain.title: Map popups cannot be dismissed with the keyboard (no close button, no Escape)
uncertain.description: Every app-rendered map popup passes closeButton={false}, and MapLibre's Popup has no built-in Escape handling (verified: no keydown/Escape in maplibre-gl/src/ui/popup.ts), so the only dismissal is a pointer click on empty map. The Map Explorer in-view list rows open popups by keyboard (good) but never close them: onActivate always sets the locId (MapExplorer.tsx:504-512) — re-activating a row with aria-pressed="true" does not toggle it off, so the pressed state is also a one-way lie. Affected popups: SightingMarkers.tsx:111, HotspotMarkers.tsx:141, TargetMarkers.tsx:79, SightingsMap.tsx:61, BirdingStats.tsx:875. A stuck-open popup overlays the map and inserts extra tab stops (eBird links inside it). The AtlasLayer popup (AtlasLayer.tsx:205) is the one that keeps the default close button — proving the styled close button is available.
uncertain.fix: Either re-enable closeButton (MapLibre renders a real <button aria-label="Close popup">, already themed via .maplibregl-popup-content CSS), or add an Escape keydown handler that clears the selection state, and make in-view list rows toggle (activating the already-selected row calls onSelect(null)). Any one of these resolves it; the row toggle also fixes the aria-pressed semantics.

uncertain.title: Atlas block popup is only openable by pointer click on the GL fill layer
uncertain.description: The California atlas block popup (block name, code, and the link to the eBird Atlas portal for that block) opens solely via map.on('click', 'sr-atlas-fill', …) — a canvas hit-test with no DOM focus path. Unlike the sighting pins, hotspots, and targets, there is no keyboard-accessible in-view list for atlas blocks, so the block-details/atlas-portal-link functionality is unavailable without a pointer. The atlas TOGGLE switches themselves are fine (real role="switch" buttons).
uncertain.fix: Add a capped "Atlas blocks in view" entry path mirroring InViewMarkerList (rows open the same block popup), or at minimum a keyboard-reachable control that opens the block containing the map center. Update ACCESSIBILITY.md's map-markers section accordingly when fixed.

uncertain.title: WelcomeScreen modal has no focus trap; map fullscreen overlay leaves hidden chrome tabbable
uncertain.description: WelcomeScreen declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and handles only Escape (line 21) — there is no Tab containment and the app behind it is not inert, so tabbing past "Explore the app first" moves focus into the fully obscured app underneath (the overlay background is opaque var(--sr-bg)); a sighted keyboard user loses the focus indicator entirely while aria-modal simultaneously tells screen readers the background doesn't exist. The map fullscreen mode has the same background-tabbing issue: it is a CSS overlay (panel fixed inset 0, App.tsx:1031-1042) and only body scroll is locked (App.tsx:390-395), so the tab bar and footer remain in the tab order while visually covered. (Not a 2.1.2 trap — focus can always leave — but focus lands on invisible controls.)
uncertain.fix: Give WelcomeScreen the same Tab-wrap handler HelpDocs uses (HelpDocs.tsx:256-274). For map fullscreen, set inert (or aria-hidden + tabindex management) on the sibling app chrome while active, and consider Escape-to-exit-fullscreen as polish.

uncertain.title: Map Explorer mobile filter focus trap snapshots focusables once — focus can escape as content changes
uncertain.description: The mobile filter sidebar trap queries focusable elements once when the overlay opens and captures first/last in the closure (lines 192-196). The sidebar's content is highly dynamic — the Filters accordion expands, the hotspot legend and in-view marker lists appear after a fetch and update on every pan/zoom, Show-all reveals rows. Once elements exist after the stale `last`, Tab from the actual last element is not intercepted and focus walks out of the modal into the backdrop-covered page; elements past the stale `last` are also skipped by the wrap. Escape + focus return (lines 200-203) work correctly. HelpDocs already implements the correct pattern (re-query inside the keydown handler, HelpDocs.tsx:261-263).
uncertain.fix: Move the querySelectorAll inside handleKeyDown so first/last reflect the live DOM on every Tab press, matching HelpDocs.tsx.

uncertain.title: In-page jump links scroll the view but never move keyboard focus
uncertain.description: The Statistics "Jump to section" nav (9 anchors) calls e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and LifeList's "media comments" anchor does the same (LifeList.tsx:505). preventDefault suppresses the browser's native sequential-focus relocation for fragment navigation, and the scroll targets are plain divs without tabindex="-1" (e.g. MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40), so after "jumping" a keyboard user's focus is still on the link at the top — the next Tab continues from the nav and they must traverse every control between anyway. The jump feature is effectively visual-only for keyboard users.
uncertain.fix: After scrolling, move focus to the destination: give each section container tabindex={-1} and call el.focus({ preventScroll: true }) alongside smoothScrollIntoView (wrap in the existing scroll helper so all jump links inherit it).

uncertain.title: Inline `outline: 'none'` on ~20 inputs/selects suppresses the designed focus ring app-wide
uncertain.description: One repeated pattern: form controls styled with inline `outline: 'none'`, which overrides the global input ring (globals.css:556-563, `outline: 2px solid var(--sr-accent)`). The only surviving indicator is the rule's `border-color: var(--sr-accent) !important` (stylesheet !important still beats inline) plus a 12%-alpha shadow — a 1.5px gray→green border tint instead of the designed 2px ring, easy to miss in dense filter sidebars, and weaker than ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs'. Locations: lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:27 (SELECT_STYLE shared by all Map Explorer selects); MapExplorer.tsx:88,690,692,863,865,1184; LifeList.tsx:627,653,667; BreedingCodeList.tsx:388,419,435; SpeciesDetail.tsx:518,613,638,652,1273; Checklists.tsx:170,265; MediaCommentsSection.tsx:75; Settings.tsx:435,1219,1231,1243. Technically still a visible state change (so not a hard 2.4.7 fail), but a significant app-wide degradation versus the global design.
uncertain.fix: Remove every inline `outline: 'none'` from inputs/selects — the global stylesheet already suppresses the default ring on non-focus-visible states and supplies the 2px accent ring on focus. The per-element onFocus borderColor handlers (e.g. Settings.tsx:437) become redundant and can stay or go.

uncertain.title: Bird-name links replace the standard focus ring with only a color change + underline
uncertain.wcag: 2.4.7 Focus Visible AA (weak indicator; 2.4.13 Focus Appearance fail forward-looking)
uncertain.description: `.sr-birdname-link:hover, .sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; outline: none; }` — the class rule out-specifies the global `button:focus-visible` outline, so the most common interactive element in the app (every species name in Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, Map Explorer, Statistics, comparer rows) shows only a green tint + underline on keyboard focus, identical to the mouse hover style. In a dense table of hundreds of rows this is materially harder to track than the 3px ring used everywhere else, and it weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim of a 'clear green outline' wherever focus lands. The global rule's faint 12% box-shadow still applies but contributes almost nothing.
uncertain.fix: Split the selector: keep `outline: none` for :hover only, and let :focus-visible keep (or restore) the global outline alongside the color/underline — e.g. `.sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; }` with no outline override.

uncertain.title: Map fullscreen overlay: no Escape exit and focus tabs into content obscured behind the overlay
uncertain.wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (also 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum, WCAG 2.2 AA)
uncertain.description: Fullscreen turns the Map Explorer tabpanel into `position: fixed; inset: 0; zIndex: 1200` (App.tsx:1031-1034) with body scroll locked (App.tsx:390-395), but no keydown handler exits it (grep confirms no Escape handler in App.tsx; the only Escape handlers in the app are the sidebar trap, HelpDocs, the combobox, TabNav, WelcomeScreen). The page chrome (tab bar, footer links, other panels' controls) stays in the DOM and in the tab order BEHIND the overlay, so a keyboard user who tabs past the map's controls watches focus vanish under the map — the focus indicator is rendered but fully obscured. Exit is possible only by finding the Exit-fullscreen FAB again. Escape is the universally expected exit for a viewport-takeover, and the obscured-focus walk is disorienting.
uncertain.fix: While mapFullscreen: add a document keydown listener that exits on Escape (returning focus to the fullscreen toggle), and apply `inert` to the app shell siblings (or trap Tab within the fullscreen panel) so focus cannot land behind the overlay.

uncertain.title: Help overlay closes without restoring focus to the control that opened it
uncertain.description: HelpDocs correctly focuses its Close button on open and traps Tab (re-querying per keydown — the best trap in the codebase), but on close (Escape at line 257 or the Close button) the overlay unmounts with focus inside it and nothing restores focus: App.tsx:1205 is just `onClose={() => setHelpOpen(false)}`. Focus drops to <body>, so a keyboard user who opened Help from the footer Help button, Settings' 'Open help', or the Welcome screen must Tab from the top of the document to get back to where they were. Standard dialog behavior is to return focus to the invoking element.
uncertain.fix: Capture `document.activeElement` when helpOpen becomes true (or pass an opener ref) and `.focus()` it after the overlay unmounts; same for the Welcome-screen-opened case.

uncertain.title: One-shot buttons unmount on activation, dropping keyboard focus to <body>
uncertain.description: Repeated pattern: a focused control disappears when activated, resetting focus to the document body so the keyboard user's next Tab restarts from the top of the page. Locations: 'Show all N' one-shot buttons rendered behind `{!showAll && ...}` — Checklists.tsx:205 (comments) and :718 (checklist rows), MediaCommentsSection.tsx:159, SpeciesDetail.tsx:1347 (species comments); and Settings KeyRow Save/Cancel — Settings.tsx:457 (Cancel) and the post-save `setEditing(false)` at :973 unmount the editing row that contains the focused button. (The toggle-style variants that stay mounted — SpeciesDetail locations/co-occurrence, BirdingStats counties — are fine and are the model to copy.)
uncertain.fix: Either keep the button mounted as a toggle ('Show fewer'), or on activation move focus explicitly — e.g. focus the first newly revealed row, or for KeyRow focus the Edit button that replaces the editor.

uncertain.title: Species combobox Escape blurs the input, stranding focus on <body>
uncertain.description: The Escape branch of the combobox keydown closes the listbox and then deliberately calls `.blur()` on the input: `(e.target as HTMLInputElement).blur()`. Per the ARIA combobox pattern, Escape should close the popup and KEEP focus in the input (a second Escape may clear it). Blurring sends focus to <body>, so a keyboard user dismissing the list loses their place entirely and must Tab back from the top of the page. The blur also exists to suppress the onFocus auto-open (line 481-485 reopens on focus), which compounds the problem: refocusing the input to continue reopens the dropdown whether wanted or not.
uncertain.fix: Drop the `.blur()` and keep focus in the input; guard the onFocus auto-open with a 'just closed via Escape' flag (or only auto-open on user input/ArrowDown) instead of throwing focus away.

uncertain.title: Tab key in the collapsed nav dropdown unmounts the focused option before the browser moves focus
uncertain.description: In TabDropdown, the menu's Tab case calls `close(false)` without preventDefault, intending the browser to move focus onward naturally. But focus lives on a menu option (real DOM focus, line 176/182), and React 18 flushes the discrete keydown update synchronously — the listbox (rendered behind `{open && ...}`, line 265) unmounts and the focused option is removed BEFORE the browser performs the default Tab traversal. Focus falls to <body>, so the default Tab then lands on the first focusable element in the document instead of the control after the trigger. On narrow/mobile widths this dropdown is the app's primary navigation, so Tab-to-leave silently teleports keyboard users to the top of the page. (Escape, by contrast, correctly returns focus to the trigger via close(true).)
uncertain.fix: On Tab: `e.preventDefault(); close(true)` then let the user Tab from the trigger — or preventDefault and programmatically focus the element after the trigger. Either keeps focus deterministic.

uncertain.title: Map popups have no close button and never manage focus for the links inside them
uncertain.description: All five MapLibre popups are rendered with `closeButton={false}` and contain real focusable eBird links: map/HotspotMarkers.tsx:141, map/SightingMarkers.tsx:111, map/TargetMarkers.tsx:79, SightingsMap.tsx:61, BirdingStats.tsx:875. When a popup is opened from the keyboard-accessible sidebar lists, focus stays on the sidebar row — the popup's links are only reachable by tabbing through the intervening map chrome, and there is no keyboard affordance to dismiss the popup. Worse, the popup is a single state-driven instance: selecting another row, clicking the map, or panning unmounts it, and if a link inside had focus, focus is dropped to <body>. (The sidebar rows carry equivalent aria-labeled eBird links, which keeps this from being serious — the popup is a redundant path — but the focus drop on unmount is still a real degradation.)
uncertain.fix: When a popup opens from a sidebar row, optionally move focus to the popup's first link and return it to the row on close; at minimum, before unmounting a popup check if document.activeElement is inside it and restore focus to the owning row/control. Consider closeButton for parity.

uncertain.title: Sortable column headers are focusable <th> with no interactive role
uncertain.description: Sortable headers are <th tabIndex={0} onClick onKeyDown> with aria-sort (LifeListTable.tsx:188-250, BreedingCodeTable.tsx:120-160). aria-sort updates correctly, but the element exposes role columnheader only — nothing announces it as an activatable control, so a screen-reader user tabbing onto "Entries" or "NB" hears a plain column header and has no cue that Enter/Space re-sorts. The BreedingCodeTable code headers additionally expose only the terse code (e.g. "NB") as the name, with the expansion in title only.
uncertain.fix: Put a real <button> inside each sortable <th> (th keeps aria-sort, button carries the label e.g. "Sort by Entries"); for breeding-code columns give the button an aria-label with the code's full label.

uncertain.title: Collapsed dropdown nav orphans every tabpanel (dangling aria-labelledby, no tablist)
uncertain.description: All panels in App.tsx use aria-labelledby="tab-{id}" (e.g. App.tsx:590). In the collapsed TabDropdown mode the id="tab-{id}" elements exist only on the listbox options while the menu is open (TabNav.tsx:298) — with the menu closed (the normal state) the visible role="tabpanel" references a nonexistent id and there is no tablist/tab anywhere in the tree, so the tab/tabpanel relationship ACCESSIBILITY.md claims ("Tabs and their panels are linked with the correct tab/tabpanel roles") is broken precisely for the zoom/narrow-viewport users who get the dropdown. The dropdown also replaces tab semantics with listbox semantics, leaving orphaned tabpanels.
uncertain.fix: Give panels a stable label that doesn't depend on the bar variant — e.g. aria-label={TAB_LABELS[id]} on each panel (or keep aria-labelledby but render persistent visually-hidden label elements), and use distinct ids for dropdown options.

uncertain.title: Entire Weather tabpanel is an aria-live aria-atomic region
uncertain.description: The whole weather panel carries aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" (App.tsx:591-592). With aria-atomic, ANY mutation — the button flipping to "Looking up…", Copy → "Copied!", the tide box changing state — re-announces the entire panel content (label, help text, full weather <pre>, tide section). The nested role="alert" (:720) and role="status" elements (:837-845) inside the live region then announce the same changes a second time. Screen-reader users get long duplicate read-outs after every interaction on the default tab.
uncertain.fix: Remove aria-live/aria-atomic from the tabpanel; rely on the existing scoped role="alert"/role="status" children, and add a small persistent polite region for "Weather copied to clipboard" if needed.

uncertain.title: Update-check outcomes are not reliably announced ('available' and 'error' not at all)
uncertain.description: The footer update checker swaps conditionally-rendered spans per state. 'checking' (:1148), 'up-to-date' (:1154) and 'downloading' (:1180) have aria-live="polite" but each span MOUNTS already containing its text — newly-inserted live regions with initial content are inconsistently announced by AT. The two states that matter most, 'available' (:1156-1178, with its Install update button) and 'error' (:1190), have no live semantics at all, so a screen-reader user who activates "Check For Updates" may hear nothing whatsoever.
uncertain.fix: Render ONE persistent <span aria-live="polite"> in the footer and change its text content across all update states, instead of mounting/unmounting per-state spans.

uncertain.title: Map Explorer async error messages are silent to assistive tech
uncertain.description: The hotspot search error (:1006-1011) and media-targets search error (:1227-1232) render as plain styled divs after an async failure — no role="alert" or aria-live, so a screen-reader user who pressed "Find Hotspots"/"Find Recent Sightings" gets no feedback that the request failed (the role="status" loading chip just disappears). Other error paths in the app do this correctly (ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, App.tsx:720, DropZone.tsx:132).
uncertain.fix: Add role="alert" to both error divs (matching ChecklistComparer's pattern).

uncertain.title: role="radio" groups in Settings have no arrow-key behavior or roving tabindex
uncertain.description: Theme (:119-128), Text size (:519-525), and Date format (:586-591) use role="radiogroup"/role="radio" with aria-checked, but every radio is a tabIndex={0} button and arrow keys do nothing. The radio role contract tells SR users "radio button, 1 of 3 — use arrow keys"; pressing arrows is a no-op, and Tab walks through each radio as a separate stop. Operable but misleading — the role advertises an interaction model the widget doesn't implement.
uncertain.fix: Either implement the radiogroup pattern (roving tabindex + ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down + Home/End), or swap to plain buttons with aria-pressed (matching SortSeg) which matches the actual Tab-based interaction.

uncertain.title: Marker-kind sr-only labels are nested inside aria-hidden and never reach AT
uncertain.description: In InViewMarkerList — the documented keyboard/SR alternative to the GL map pins — the colored kind dot is CONTAINING {getDotLabel(item)}. aria-hidden removes the entire subtree from the accessibility tree, including the sr-only text, so the hotspot kind / recency information conveyed by dot color is announced to no one. ACCESSIBILITY.md explicitly claims "map recency dots — carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader"; the code makes that claim false.
uncertain.fix: Move the sr-only label outside the aria-hidden dot span: keep the dot aria-hidden, and render the sr-only kind label as a sibling inside the row button.

uncertain.title: ChecklistBadges convey present/absent state via aria-label on generic spans; group unnamed
uncertain.description: Each Badge is a role-less <span aria-label={presentTitle|absentTitle}>. ARIA prohibits naming on the generic role, and screen readers inconsistently honor aria-label on plain spans in browse mode — so SR users may hear only the visible "Photo Audio Video Breeding Weather Tide" text with the present/absent state (the badge's entire point) dropped. The wrapping role="group" (:53) also has no accessible name. The tests assert the aria-labels exist but can't catch the exposure problem.
uncertain.fix: Add role="img" to the Badge span (making the aria-label valid and reliably announced), and aria-label="Checklist contents" on the role="group" container.

uncertain.title: No h1, most views have no headings, and heading levels are inconsistent across tabs

uncertain.title: Disclosed chart-bar-label exception verified — but it understates the dark-theme failures (down to 1.29:1) and a working fix already exists in-code
uncertain.description: ACCESSIBILITY.md's known exception ('a few dense data-visualization labels (percentage figures printed inside saturated chart bars) do not yet meet AA in every case') is accurate in direction but materially understates scope. uncertain.title: Dark theme: map pin tokens are lightened 'for dark backgrounds' but draw on the always-light Positron basemap (1.69–2.25:1)
uncertain.description: There is no dark basemap variant (lib/mapStyle.ts tunes Positron only; no theme branch), yet the dark-theme --sr-map-* tokens lighten the pin colors: visited/heat pins #34D399 vs Positron land (~#F2F0EB) = 1.69:1, personal #E0A060 = 1.97:1, unvisited #7BA7C9 = 2.25:1 (light theme passes: 3.66–3.97:1). uncertain.title: Light theme: accent-colored text marginally fails on tinted/page backgrounds (4.03–4.32:1)
uncertain.description: Light --sr-accent #2D8653 passes on white surfaces (4.52:1) but fails where it is used on anything tinted: on --sr-accent-bg = 4.03:1 — the app-wide active-state pattern (ghost buttons, active filter pills, the tab dropdown's selected option TabNav.tsx:309-314, SpeciesPanel count badge :44-45; background:'var(--sr-accent-bg)' + accent text appears in 14 files); on --sr-bg = 4.32:1 — the active tab label (tab bar sits directly on the page background, App.tsx:583) and the footer 'Up to date' status (App.tsx:1154); on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.11:1. Dark theme passes everywhere (7.75–10.35:1).

uncertain.title: Light theme: error text on error background is just below AA (4.41:1)
uncertain.description: --sr-error #DC2626 on --sr-error-bg #FEF2F2 computes to 4.41:1 — marginally under 4.5:1 — and this pair styles every error banner and the 'negative' filter pill state: Checklists.tsx:236/488, LifeList.tsx:108/384, BreedingCodeList.tsx:196, Settings.tsx:304/480, ChecklistComparer.tsx:374, NamedBirds.tsx:108, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:186, SpeciesDetail.tsx:430, DropZone.tsx error text. uncertain.title: Light theme: muted text on tinted surfaces falls just under AA (4.27–4.40:1)
uncertain.description: --sr-text-muted #71717A passes on white (4.83:1) but not on the tinted surfaces it is commonly paired with in light theme: on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.40:1 (inactive segmented-control labels in MapSidebarUI SegControl, the basemap switcher buttons in globals.css:246, the missing-media badges in the target popup TargetMarkers.tsx:92, numerous chips); on --sr-quote-bg = 4.27:1 (Named Birds comment block); on --sr-accent-bg = 4.31:1 (secondary text inside selected rows, e.g. the location line of a selected Nearest Targets row, MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317). uncertain.title: ToggleSwitch off-state track is nearly invisible in light theme (1.48:1)
uncertain.description: The off-state track uses --sr-gray-400 (#D4D4D8): 1.48:1 against the white button surface AND 1.48:1 against the white knob, so the knob position — the visual state indicator of every 'merge subspecies' / 'show spuh' / 'hide weather' switch — is barely discernible in light theme (the on state passes: accent track 4.52:1 vs surface). Dark theme: track vs surface 2.29:1 (also <3:1) though knob-vs-track passes (7.73:1). aria-checked is correct for AT, but the sighted off/on distinction fails non-text contrast.

uncertain.title: Form-control borders are far below non-text contrast (1.19–1.34:1)
uncertain.description: --sr-border (#E4E4E7 light / #27272A dark) is the only boundary cue on text inputs, selects, date inputs and unselected pills throughout the app (SELECT_STYLE here; the same '1px/1.5px solid var(--sr-border)' pattern on inputs in MapExplorer, Checklists, LifeList, Settings, SpeciesDetail). Computed: 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark vs surface, 1.21:1 / 1.34:1 vs page bg; even --sr-border-medium is 1.73:1 light / 1.70:1 dark. Inputs whose extent is identified only by this border fail 1.4.11; the focus ring fixes it only once focused.

uncertain.title: 'Personal Location' popup badge fails in light theme (2.90:1)
uncertain.description: The hotspot popup's 'Personal Location' badge sets --sr-map-personal (#C9842A) text on --sr-is-target-bg (#FFF7ED): 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 (dark passes, 8.38:1). The pin color token was designed as a map fill, not a text color.

uncertain.title: DropZone error state's border and icon are nearly invisible (1.74–1.90:1)
uncertain.description: In the error state the drop zone's border and upload icon switch to --sr-error-muted (#FCA5A5 light): 1.74:1 against the --sr-error-bg fill and 1.90:1 against the surrounding surface, so the state-change boundary/icon fails non-text contrast (dark: icon vs surface 2.74:1; vs error-bg 3.02:1 passes). uncertain.title: ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim is broader than the computed reality
uncertain.description: The published statement says text, buttons, links, map popups and form controls 'meet the WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standard (4.5:1) in both the light and dark themes', with chart-bar labels as the only known exception. Computed counterexamples outside that exception: light-theme active pills/links on tinted backgrounds 4.03–4.41:1 (accent-on-accent-bg, error-on-error-bg, active tab on page bg), --sr-text-disabled used on content at 2.29–2.56:1, dark-theme target chips at 1.52–1.92:1, dark-theme breeding pills at 1.97–2.94:1, and form-control borders at 1.19–1.27:1 (non-text).
