uncertain.fix: Either fix the token-level failures in this report (most are 1-line token edits) and keep the claim, or temporarily widen the known-exceptions paragraph to honestly cover active-state tints in light theme and chip/pill labels in dark theme.

uncertain.title: Media count badges in checklist comparer use aria-label on a generic <span> — info silently lost to screen readers
uncertain.description: MediaIcons renders per-species photo/audio/video presence as lucide SVG icons inside a plain <span aria-label={`${n} ${label}`}>. ARIA prohibits naming on role=generic, so most browser/SR pairs ignore the aria-label, and the SVGs themselves have no text alternative — the media information (which types exist and counts) is conveyed to sighted users only. The same file's Checklists tab equivalent (Checklists.tsx:276 Badge) does this correctly with role="img", and ChecklistBadges.tsx is correct too — this one component missed the pattern.
uncertain.fix: Add role="img" to the span (matching the Badge pattern in Checklists.tsx:276) so the aria-label is exposed: <span role="img" aria-label={`${n} ${label}`} ...>.

uncertain.title: Repeated "↗" checklist links named only by the arrow glyph
uncertain.wcag: 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) A / 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA
uncertain.description: Three Statistics sections render external eBird checklist links whose only content is the character "↗" with title="Open checklist": the effort superlative cards (line 1332), single-checklist-bird chips (line 1564), and one-and-done bird chips (line 1589). The accessible name is computed from content, so every one of these (potentially dozens in the chip lists) is announced as "north east arrow, link" or skipped entirely depending on SR symbol verbosity — identical and non-descriptive. title only provides a description, not the name, when content exists.
uncertain.fix: Add aria-label, e.g. aria-label={`Open eBird checklist ${bird.submissionId} for ${bird.name} (opens in a new tab)`}, mirroring NamedBirdRow.tsx:94 which already does this correctly, and mark the glyph aria-hidden.

uncertain.title: Missing-media type icons in Media Targets popup and marker chips have no text alternative anywhere
uncertain.description: The whole point of a media target is which media types (photo/audio/video) the user is missing, but that information is conveyed exclusively by unnamed inline SVGs: in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97, bare <svg> per missing type, no aria-hidden, no label), in the on-map chip labels (TargetMarkers.tsx:62, MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML), and the keyboard-accessible "Nearest Targets" sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:~1315-1318) show only name/location/distance — they omit missing types entirely. A screen-reader user can find a target but never learn which media it is missing. This also weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that icon-only information "carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader."
uncertain.fix: In the popup, give each type span role="img" aria-label={`Missing ${t.toLowerCase()}`} (or append sr-only text) and aria-hidden the SVGs; add the missing types as text (visible or sr-only) to the Nearest Targets sidebar rows so the keyboard/SR path carries the full information.

uncertain.title: DOM map markers (Species Detail / Named Birds pins, target chips, Statistics rank pins) are unnamed, role-less click targets invisible to AT
uncertain.wcag: 1.1.1 Non-text Content A / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A
uncertain.description: ACCESSIBILITY.md documents sidebar-list alternatives for the Map Explorer's GPU canvas markers, but the DOM <Marker> maps have no equivalent treatment: SightingsMap.tsx:55-58 renders each pin as a clickable <div> containing an innerHTML SVG with no role, name, or tabindex; TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 does the same for target chips; BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 for the Statistics RankIcon pins (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101, an unnamed SVG). Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot perceive or activate any of these markers or reach their popups. Impact is moderated because equivalent data exists in adjacent text on most surfaces (Named Birds rows list every sighting date/location/checklist; Species Detail has Top Locations and per-sighting lists; Statistics has top-location tables), but the popup-only details (e.g. per-coordinate date groupings) have no named path.
uncertain.fix: Make the Marker child a real button: role="button", tabIndex=0, aria-label like `${locName ?? coordinate}, ${sightings.length} sightings` with Enter/Space handling — or explicitly scope the ACCESSIBILITY.md marker claim and guarantee a text equivalent exists beside every DOM-marker map.

uncertain.title: Placeholder-only (or format-only) accessible names on text inputs; Map Explorer From/To dates are indistinguishable
uncertain.wcag: 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA / 1.3.1 Info and Relationships A
uncertain.description: Several inputs have no label or aria-label, so the accessible name falls back to the placeholder. Worst case: the Map Explorer date-range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862,864) both have placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD" — a SR user hears the format string twice with nothing distinguishing From vs To (the visible "Date Range" SidebarLabel is not programmatically associated). Same pattern: MapExplorer.tsx:84 (place search), 689/691 (Latitude/Longitude), 1182 (target species search); Settings.tsx:1216/1228/1240 map-default inputs, whose visible "Latitude"/"Longitude"/"Radius (mi)" labels are unassociated <div>s so the computed name is "e.g. 37.8275"; SpeciesDetail.tsx:1268 and MediaCommentsSection.tsx:70 comment filters (placeholder is at least descriptive there, but disappears once text is typed for sighted users). Contrast: Checklists.tsx:655/663 date inputs do it right with aria-label="From date"/"To date".
uncertain.fix: Add aria-label to each (e.g. "From date (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "To date (YYYY-MM-DD)", "Latitude", "Longitude", "Search by place name"), or associate the existing visible labels via htmlFor/id.

uncertain.title: Placeholder is the only label on search/filter, coordinate, and API-key text inputs
uncertain.description: These text inputs have no label or aria-label; their only identification is the placeholder, which disappears as soon as the user types (and browsers' placeholder→accessible-name fallback is a last resort, not a reliable label). Locations: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-70 ('Filter media comments…'); Checklists.tsx:161-165 (shared CommentSearchBox, placeholders 'Filter checklist comments…' / 'Filter species comments…' at :544/:555); SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1268 ('Filter comments…'); MapExplorer.tsx:82-84 ('Search by place name'), :689/:691 (Latitude/Longitude number inputs — after entry a sighted user sees two bare numbers with nothing saying which is which), :1182-1184 ('Search species…'); Settings.tsx:424-428 (API key entry, 'Paste your API key' — the row label at :352 is an unassociated <div>). Impact is worst for low-vision and cognitive users mid-entry, and for the lat/lng pair where the only differentiator vanishes.
uncertain.fix: Add aria-label to each input (e.g. aria-label="Filter media comments", aria-label="Latitude", aria-label="eBird API key") while keeping the placeholder as a hint; for the Map Explorer lat/lng pair, prefer small visible labels like the Settings map-defaults section already has.

uncertain.title: Atlas block popups are pointer-only — no keyboard route to open them
uncertain.description: Atlas block info popups open exclusively via a MapLibre map.on('click','sr-atlas-fill') handler on the GL fill layer (AtlasLayer.tsx:109-132). There is no sidebar list, search, or other focusable path to a block, so the popup's content — block name, the eBird atlas portal link, and 'Highest breeding code … N of your breeding records in this block' — is unreachable without a pointer. The breeding data shown in the popup is not surfaced anywhere else in the app (the sidebar legend only explains tier colors). The popup JSX itself is fine (escaped, keeps the default labeled close button), but keyboard users can never open it.
uncertain.fix: When shading is on, add a focusable 'Shaded blocks in view' sidebar list (mirroring InViewMarkerList — blocksInBounds already provides viewport-scoped blocks and breedingByBlock the per-block data) whose rows open the same popup; or expose a block search/jump input. Cap + hint like the other lists.

uncertain.title: Map sidebar filter inputs rely on placeholders for their accessible names; date inputs are named 'YYYY-MM-DD'
uncertain.wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions A)
uncertain.description: The Map Explorer sidebar inputs have no <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby — the SidebarLabel headings are unassociated styled divs. Accessible names therefore fall back to placeholders: the two Date Range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862-865) both compute to the meaningless, identical name "YYYY-MM-DD" (a screen-reader user cannot tell From from To, or that they are date filters at all); Latitude/Longitude (:689-692), "Search by place name" (:86), and "Search species…" (:1182) are intelligible but vanish once a value is typed. The adjacent Search button (:90-103) has only a title attribute for its name.
uncertain.fix: Add aria-label="Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)" (and aria-labels echoing the other placeholders), or give SidebarLabel an id and reference it via aria-labelledby plus a per-field qualifier. Give the search icon button aria-label="Search". (Flagging here because these gate the map experience; may overlap with a forms-dimension audit.)

uncertain.title: Map chrome text inherits MapLibre's fixed `font: 12px/20px Helvetica` — does not scale with the in-app Text Size control
uncertain.description:
maplibre-gl.css (imported at SnowMap.tsx:7) sets `.maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,…}`. The app's `.maplibregl-popup-content` override in globals.css:568 themes colors but sets no font-size or family, so any map-rendered text without an explicit rem size stays at a hard 12px Helvetica regardless of the Text Size setting. Affected: (1) the AtlasLayer block popup title — `
{sel.name}
` at AtlasLayer.tsx:213 and the linked variant at :208-211 have no fontSize; (2) the attribution credits on every map (SnowMap.tsx:121 `attributionControl={{ compact: true }}` — provider links render at fixed 12px when expanded); (3) the AtlasLayer popup's default close button (it is the only popup that doesn't pass `closeButton={false}`, so users get maplibre's small fixed-size '×' — also a WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size concern). This matters more here than in a typical web app: ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 states the Text Size control is "especially useful in the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own", so on desktop this text is genuinely un-resizable. All other popups (SightingMarkers, HotspotMarkers, TargetMarkers, SightingsMap, the BirdingStats geo popup) set explicit rem sizes and are fine.
uncertain.fix: In globals.css extend the existing popup override: `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`; give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize; pass `closeButton={false}` on the AtlasLayer popup for consistency with the other four popups (its onClose path already exists).

uncertain.title: Fixed-pixel text geometry in Statistics overlaps or clips at 200% text scale (pattern, multiple locations)
uncertain.wcag: 1.4.4 Resize Text AA (clipping cases also 1.4.12 Text Spacing AA)
uncertain.description: One repeating pattern: rem-sized text placed in fixed-pixel boxes that don't grow with the text. (1) BarRow (statsPrimitives.tsx:59-75): label column `width: labelWidth, flexShrink: 0` and value column `width: pctOf ? 68 : 40`, no overflow handling — at 200% scale, labels ("Jan" at labelWidth=28: BirdingStats.tsx:754,794,829; "SnowRaven weather" at 120: BirdingStats.tsx:1425-1429; MediaStatsSections.tsx:180-182,294) and values like "1,234 (56%)" are ~2× wider than their boxes and overlap the adjacent bar graphic. (2) Stacked-bar % labels inside fixed-height `overflow: hidden` segments — BirdingStats.tsx:1122-1133 and 1173-1185 (height 32, fits 200%) but the protocol sub-bars at 1151-1158 are `height: 20` with 0.625rem labels: at 200% the 20px glyphs (30px line box) clip vertically; same construction in the media bars at 1356, 1380, 1401. (3) Hard-ellipsized name columns `width: 100`/`width: 96` + nowrap+hidden (BirdingStats.tsx:953, 984, 1028, 1057) — county/species names truncate to a few characters at 200% with only a mouse-only `title` as recovery. (4) Donut center captions absolutely centered in fixed 120/132px charts — BirdingStats.tsx:764-769, 804-807 and MediaStatsSections.tsx:58-61 — at 200% the caption (e.g. "September" ≈140px wide, or a 1.25rem count) spills across the donut ring on both sides. Screen-reader users are unaffected (the role="img" aria-labels carry the data); this degrades the visual rendering for sighted low-vision users at 150-200%.
uncertain.fix: Convert the fixed widths to rem (e.g. labelWidth 28→'2.5rem', value column '4.5rem') or `minWidth` + `flex-basis`; change the sub-bar `height: 20` to `minHeight: 20` (the % label centers itself, the bar just grows); for the donut captions either size the chart in rem or cap centerValue/centerLabel with a clamp().

uncertain.title: List Comparer summary bars and result panels don't reflow at 320px — labels truncate to identical text
uncertain.description: Both comparer results screens use rigid column counts with no narrow-width collapse. The five-cell summary (`gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(5, 1fr)'` — ResultsView.tsx:111 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:281) gives each cell ~58px at 320px; the 0.625rem uppercase labels are `whiteSpace: nowrap; overflow: hidden; textOverflow: ellipsis` (ResultsView.tsx:165-173, ChecklistComparer.tsx:478), so "Checklist A" and "Checklist B" (and "<name> total" pairs) ellipsize to identical strings — the numbers become indistinguishable at that width. Below them, ResultsView.tsx:129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` species panels and ChecklistComparer.tsx:310 `1fr 1fr` A-only/B-only panels never stack, leaving ~90-140px columns where species names wrap to 4+ lines. Nothing scrolls two-dimensionally and the panel headers repeat the counts, so it is degraded rather than lost — but the summary labels' ambiguity is a concrete information loss at 320px.
uncertain.fix: Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` for the stat bars (cells wrap to two rows on narrow screens), and collapse the panel grids to one column under 640px (reuse the `.sr-two-col` media-query pattern from globals.css:601).

uncertain.title: 'Nearest Targets' list is not scoped to the map view and does not update on pan/zoom, contrary to the statement
uncertain.description: ACCESSIBILITY.md says the Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list 'works the same way' as the in-view lists and then asserts 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom (very dense views are capped, with a "zoom in to narrow the list" hint).' The keyboard path itself is real (each row has a focusable, aria-labelled locate button at lines 1320-1333 that opens the same popup and pans). But `nearest10` (lines 453-461) is computed as the 10 closest pins to the SEARCH CENTER lat/lng inputs — it ignores `mapBounds`, never reacts to panning or zooming, and has no over-cap hint. Only the 'Sightings in view' and 'Hotspots in view' lists (markersInView + mapBounds, cap 200, MapSidebarUI.tsx:118-121) match the published description. A screen-reader user following the statement would expect the targets keyboard list to track the viewport; it doesn't.
uncertain.fix: Either scope the targets list with markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) like the other two lists, or correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the 10 nearest to the search center.

uncertain.title: Tab Layout reordering is mouse/touch-only with no keyboard alternative — the statement's keyboard section discloses no exceptions
uncertain.wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (also WCAG 2.2 2.5.7 Dragging Movements AA)
uncertain.description: Settings → Tab Layout reorders tabs exclusively via HTML5 drag-and-drop on the <li> rows; the 'drag handle' is a non-focusable plain <div> carrying an aria-label (which is also invalid ARIA on a generic div — it won't be announced), and there is no keyboard mechanism (no move-up/move-down buttons, no arrow-key handling). The app itself admits this in an sr-only note at Settings.tsx:699 ('Keyboard reordering is not supported in this version'), and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'Nearly all of SnowRaven is reachable and operable with the keyboard alone' hedge technically covers it — but the Keyboard Navigation section enumerates zero exceptions, so a reader has no way to learn this feature is keyboard-inaccessible. Show/hide toggles are keyboard-accessible; ordering is not achievable at all without a pointer, which is a hard 2.1.1 failure for that function (and a 2.5.7 Dragging Movements failure under WCAG 2.2).
uncertain.fix: Add keyboard reordering (focusable handle button with ArrowUp/ArrowDown + aria-live position announcements, or per-row Move up/Move down buttons), and until then name this exception explicitly in ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard section.

uncertain.title: Closing the Help overlay drops focus to <body> instead of returning to the Help button
uncertain.description: HelpDocs correctly focuses its Close button on open and traps Tab, but onClose (Close button or Escape) simply unmounts the overlay (App.tsx:1203-1205 just sets helpOpen false) — focus falls to document.body and the keyboard user restarts from the top of the page. The Map Explorer filter sidebar (filtersButtonRef refocus) and the TabNav dropdown (close(true)) both restore focus correctly; HelpDocs is the inconsistent one. It can be opened from three places (footer, Welcome screen, Settings), so the opener should be remembered.
uncertain.fix: Capture document.activeElement when the overlay mounts and restore focus to it in a cleanup effect (covers all three openers without prop plumbing).

uncertain.title: DropZone inline `outline: 'none'` defeats the global keyboard focus ring
uncertain.description: The DropZone (role="button", tabIndex=0 — keyboard activation itself works) sets outline: 'none' in its inline style. Inline styles override the stylesheet's [role="button"]:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--sr-accent) } rule (globals.css:546-551, no !important), leaving only the rule's faint 12%-alpha box-shadow glow as the focus indicator; the border/background highlight is driven by mouse-only isHovered state. Keyboard users on the List Comparer get an almost invisible cue on the primary upload control. (Reported here because it directly degrades keyboard operation of an otherwise-correct widget; full focus-visible sweep belongs to that dimension.)
uncertain.fix: Delete the inline outline: 'none' (the global :focus-visible ring only shows for keyboard focus, so the mouse aesthetics are unaffected), or mirror the isDragging accent border on :focus-visible.

uncertain.title: WCAG 2.2 deltas: 14×14 favicon link targets and sticky-header focus obscuring
uncertain.description: Forward-looking 2.2 items. (a) Target size: the eBird / Birds of the World favicon links rendered beside nearly every bird name are 14×14px, placed directly adjacent to each other — below the 24×24 minimum with no qualifying spacing exception; they are the most frequently repeated small target in the app. The Species Detail combobox chevron (SpeciesDetail.tsx:521, ~16px <span>) is also undersized but pointer-redundant. Most other small controls measured are compliant (close 26×26, eye 28×28, locate 26×26, FABs 36×36). (b) 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: LifeListTable's sticky header row (position: sticky, top: 0 — LifeListTable.tsx:182-187) can fully cover row links (BirdName, ML catalog) when Shift+Tab scrolls a focused element up under it; same risk for BreedingCodeTable's sticky first column (line 128).
uncertain.fix: Give the favicon anchors padding to reach a ≥24×24 hit area (visual size can stay 14px). For sticky tables, add scroll-padding-top equal to the header height on the scroll container so focused elements land below the sticky header.

uncertain.title: Tablist lacks Home/End keys (APG completeness)
uncertain.wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (advisory — APG tabs pattern; no AA failure)
uncertain.description: The desktop tab bar implements roving tabindex with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight + wrap (TabNav.tsx:109-123) but not Home/End to jump to the first/last tab, which the WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern recommends (the collapsed dropdown DOES implement Home/End at lines 197-204, so the two modes are inconsistent). With 10+ tabs this is several extra keystrokes, not a barrier — forward-looking polish only.
uncertain.fix: Add Home → items[0] and End → items[items.length-1] cases to the tablist onKeyDown, mirroring the dropdown's handling.

uncertain.title: Map Explorer Filters accordion button lacks aria-expanded
uncertain.description: The collapsible filter panel toggle in the sightings sidebar (button at :836, panel collapsed via max-height 0) exposes no expanded/collapsed state — the only cue is the rotated chevron. Every other disclosure in the app does carry aria-expanded (NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76/:440, TabNav.tsx:234).
uncertain.fix: Add aria-expanded={filterOpen} (and optionally aria-controls) to the Filters button.

uncertain.title: Comment-count live regions announce on every keystroke
uncertain.description: CommentSearchBox's match count (N comments, used by both the Checklist Comments and Species Comments sections) recomputes from the filter input on every keystroke, so a screen reader queues an "N comments" announcement per character typed, competing with character echo. The count announcement itself is good 4.1.3 practice — it just needs to settle.
uncertain.fix: Debounce the text feeding the live region (~400-500 ms after typing pauses) while leaving the visible count immediate.

uncertain.title: Comparison-mode switch uses tablist/tab roles without panels or arrow-key support
uncertain.description: The Life Lists / Checklists mode switch is role="tablist" + role="tab" aria-selected, but there is no aria-controls, no role="tabpanel" for the swapped content, no roving tabindex, and no arrow-key handling — SR users are told they're in a tab widget whose conventions (arrows move, panel follows) don't hold. Inside the app shell's real tab system, this also nests tab semantics within a tabpanel.
uncertain.fix: Either complete the pattern (ids + aria-controls + tabpanel + roving tabindex + arrows) or simplify to a role="group" of aria-pressed buttons like SortSeg.

uncertain.title: TabDropdown listbox misuses aria-activedescendant and trigger lacks aria-controls
uncertain.description: The dropdown menu manages focus by moving DOM focus to the option buttons (roving), yet the listbox container also sets aria-activedescendant — on an element that itself never receives focus (no tabindex), where the attribute has no effect, and pointing at the SELECTED tab rather than the focused option. All options are also tabIndex={0} (the pattern expects -1 with the container or roving single stop), and the trigger (:233) has aria-haspopup/aria-expanded but no aria-controls referencing the listbox. Functionally usable (DOM focus carries the announcements) but the ARIA contradicts the actual focus model.
uncertain.fix: Remove aria-activedescendant (DOM focus already tracks the active option), set option tabIndex={-1}, give the listbox an id, and add aria-controls to the trigger.

uncertain.title: Species selector chevron is a click-only unnamed <span>
uncertain.description: The open/close chevron beside the species combobox input is a <span onClick> with no role, no accessible name, and no keyboard access. The function is redundantly available (focusing the input opens the list, Escape closes), so impact is low, but it's an interactive element invisible to AT and unreachable by keyboard.
uncertain.fix: Either mark it decorative (aria-hidden, remove onClick — the input already toggles) or make it a real button with aria-label="Toggle species list" and tabIndex={-1}.

uncertain.title: role="status" loading indicators mount already containing their text (announcement unreliable)
uncertain.description: Loading/status chips are conditionally rendered elements that carry role="status" AND their message in the same insertion: TabLoading (App.tsx:125), tide states (App.tsx:837-845), MapExplorer loading chip (:1437), BirdingStats (:464, :883), AtlasLayer (:230), WeatherTidePanel (:165-235). Live regions must exist before their content changes; regions inserted with initial text are announced by some AT/browser combos and skipped by others, so loading/unavailable states are inconsistently conveyed. Pattern issue — reported once for all locations.
uncertain.fix: Keep a persistent (always-mounted, possibly empty) role="status" container per area and swap its text content, rather than mounting the live region together with its message.

uncertain.title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: sub-24px targets (species favicon links, combobox chevron)
uncertain.description: The eBird and Birds of the World favicon links rendered next to every bird name are 14×14 px targets with a 5 px gap — under the 24×24 minimum, packed in dense table rows where the spacing exception doesn't obviously hold, and they appear hundreds of times (Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, Stats). The SpeciesDetail chevron (~16 px, SpeciesDetail.tsx:521) is similar. Not a WCAG 2.1 AA failure; flagged as a 2.2 delta.
uncertain.fix: Grow the anchor hit area to ≥24×24 via padding on .sr-favicon-slot (visual size can stay 14px), and give the chevron button a 24px hit box.

uncertain.title: No active color-scheme declaration; unstyled placeholders fall below AA in dark theme (~3.85:1)
uncertain.description: The only color-scheme rule lives in src/index.css, which is dead code (main.tsx imports only globals.css), and no ::placeholder rule exists anywhere. In the app-controlled dark theme, UA defaults therefore stay light-scheme: Chrome's default placeholder (#757575) on the dark input surface #18181B computes to ≈3.85:1 (light theme passes ≈4.61:1); Firefox's 54%-opacity placeholder lands similarly marginal. 18 inputs use placeholders (search fields, date YYYY-MM-DD hints, API-key fields). Light-scheme scrollbars/native select popups in dark mode are a related cosmetic effect.
uncertain.fix: Add `color-scheme: light` to :root and `color-scheme: dark` to [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css, plus an explicit `::placeholder { color: var(--sr-text-muted); opacity: 1 }` rule (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark).

uncertain.title: Chart non-text elements below 3:1: amber line in light theme, faint bar segments, stacked-segment boundaries
uncertain.description: Computed non-text chart parts under 3:1 — light theme: the Audio series line --sr-graph-audio #F59E0B vs the white card = 2.15:1 (media-over-time chart; SightingsGraph media line too), --sr-chart-blue-light bar segment vs surface = 1.80:1, tier-1 fill vs surface = 2.64:1; the hand-built stacked breeding bar's adjacent segments: tier-2 vs tier-1 = 2.04:1 light / 1.50:1 dark, tier-4 vs tier-2 = 2.79:1 light / 2.20:1 dark (BirdingStats.tsx:1677-1679). Mitigations keeping this minor: every chart has a data-bearing role="img" label, tooltips, and most values are duplicated as text (legend counts, BarRow numerals).
uncertain.fix: Darken light --sr-graph-audio toward #B45309 (5.02:1 — already proven in --sr-age-immature), add 1px separators between stacked-bar segments, and bump light --sr-chart-blue-light/tier-1 fills toward their 3:1 neighbors.

uncertain.title: Multi-series line charts differentiated by hue alone
uncertain.description: The media-over-time chart draws four lines (photo/audio/video/total) distinguished only by stroke color, with a color-keyed legend — for color-blind users the photo (blue) vs video (purple) pair in particular is hard to separate. Tooltips name each series on hover and the role="img" summary covers AT users, so the information is reachable, but not glanceable. Same pattern wherever SightingsGraph's media chart overlays multiple series.
uncertain.fix: Add per-series strokeDasharray patterns and/or distinct dot marker shapes to the recharts <Line> elements so series differ by more than hue.

uncertain.title: Recency tier is color-alone at a glance (sighted users); the faint 'old' dot compounds it in light theme (1.64:1)
uncertain.description: The fresh/mid/old recency tiers on the Nearest Targets sidebar dots and the on-map chip backgrounds are differentiated only by color for sighted users; the sr-only labels (MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313) cover screen readers — so ACCESSIBILITY.md's specific claim about hidden labels on recency dots is TRUE — and the popup shows the tier as text ('≤7 days') plus the date, so the information is reachable by interaction. But a color-blind user scanning the list/map cannot rank targets without clicking each one, and the light-theme 'old' dot (#A8D4BB) is also only 1.64:1 against the sidebar surface (its compensating border is --sr-border at 1.27:1).
uncertain.fix: Show the visible date (already computed) or a tier letter/shape next to each sidebar dot, and give the 'old' dot a ≥3:1 border (e.g. --sr-accent-strong).

uncertain.title: 'No media' minus icon nearly invisible (1.47:1 light / 1.70:1 dark)
uncertain.description: Life List media columns render a Minus icon in --sr-gray-300 (#D1D5DB) on the white row surface = 1.47:1 (dark: #3F3F46 on #18181B = 1.70:1) to mean 'no media of this type' (repeated at lines 288, 302, 316, 331). The meaning ('zero') is inferable from the absence of a count link, which is why this is minor rather than moderate, but the chosen glyph as drawn fails non-text contrast in both themes.
uncertain.fix: Use --sr-text-disabled or --sr-border-medium darkened to ≥3:1, or render a plain '—' in --sr-text-muted (which also gives AT users something to announce).

uncertain.title: Life List species column is <td>, not a row header, unlike the Breeding Codes table
uncertain.description: BreedingCodeTable.tsx:174 correctly marks the species name cell <th scope="row">, but LifeListTable.tsx:267 uses a plain <td>. The Photo/Audio/Video count cells contain links whose only content is a bare number (e.g. "3"), so when navigating by cell or link, SRs that announce row headers would give the species context automatically in the Breeding table but not here. Column-header context still works, so impact is small.
uncertain.fix: Change the species cell to <th scope="row" style={{...textAlign:'left'}}> to match BreedingCodeTable.tsx:174.

uncertain.title: Southern-hemisphere moon emoji mirroring makes screen readers announce the wrong phase
uncertain.description: The moon-phase emoji is the ONLY carrier of moon-phase information in night weather blocks (no adjacent text line — the condition emoji, by contrast, is followed by the textual condition on the next line). For northern latitudes this is acceptable: SRs read Unicode emoji names ("waxing gibbous moon"), which match the phase. But MOON_SOUTH deliberately swaps to the visually-mirrored emoji for lat < 0, so a southern-hemisphere waxing crescent is rendered as 🌘 whose Unicode name is "waning crescent moon" — a SR (and anyone hovering for the character name) hears the opposite phase. Constrained by the paste-into-eBird output format, so an in-app-only fix is appropriate.
uncertain.fix: Where the formatted block is displayed in-app (the <pre> on the Weather tab and WeatherTidePanel), wrap the header emoji run in a span with an aria-label giving the true phase name (e.g. "cloudy, waxing crescent moon"), or append the phase as text in the in-app rendering only.

uncertain.title: Settings radiogroups use role=radio without the expected arrow-key behavior
uncertain.wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (ARIA radiogroup pattern) AA
uncertain.description: The Color theme (:119), Text size (:519), and Date format (:586) groups are role="radiogroup" containing role="radio" buttons that are all tabIndex={0}. Screen readers announce them as radio buttons (e.g. "radio, 1 of 4") and instruct arrow-key navigation, but arrow keys do nothing and unchecked radios remain in the Tab order — behavior that contradicts the announced role. Users can still operate everything with Tab+Enter, so impact is confusion rather than blockage.
uncertain.fix: Either implement the radiogroup pattern (roving tabindex + ArrowLeft/Right to move checked state) or downgrade to the house pattern used elsewhere: plain buttons with aria-pressed inside role="group" aria-label.

uncertain.title: Species selector dropdown toggle chevron is a mouse-only <span>
uncertain.description: The chevron that opens/closes the species combobox list is a <span onClick> with no role, name, or tab stop. Keyboard users are not blocked (the input opens the listbox on focus and Escape closes it), but a pointer-AT or switch user targeting the visible affordance gets a dead control, and it is invisible to screen readers.
uncertain.fix: Either mark it aria-hidden="true" (treating it as decorative since the input itself toggles the list), or make it a real <button tabIndex={-1} aria-label="Toggle species list"> per the ARIA combobox pattern.

uncertain.title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: several form controls are under the 24px minimum target size
uncertain.description: Forward-looking 2.2 delta only. The atlas overlay role="switch" buttons are 38x22px (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under the 24px minimum), and several zero-padding text buttons are ~16-18px tall: the API-key Show/Hide button (Settings.tsx:363-373, padding 0, 0.75rem text), the 'Clear filter' underline buttons (LifeList.tsx:694-703, Checklists.tsx:685-690, SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667), and the 'Go to Settings →' banner buttons (App.tsx:611-619, padding 0). Most currently escape 2.5.8 via the spacing exception (no adjacent target within 24px), but that is fragile under layout changes and the small targets are already hard for motor-impaired users under 2.1 best practice.
uncertain.fix: Bump the switch buttons to at least 24px tall (e.g. 44x24 track) and give the zero-padding text buttons enough padding (or min-height: 24px with negative-margin compensation) to reach a 24x24 hit area.

uncertain.title: WCAG 2.2: 12px icon-only eBird link in Nearest Unvisited Hotspots rows is below Target Size minimum
uncertain.description: The external eBird link in each 'Nearest Unvisited Hotspots' row is an inline-flex anchor whose only content is a 12px ExternalLink icon with no padding, giving a ~12-14px hit target packed between the location-name button and the distance text — below the 24x24 CSS px minimum of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 and a genuinely hard touch/low-motor target. (For comparison, the equivalent crosshair locate buttons at :1326-1330 are 26x26 and pass.)
uncertain.fix: Give the anchor a fixed 24x24 (or 26x26 to match the crosshair buttons) box with centered icon, e.g. width/height 24 + justifyContent center.

uncertain.title: Boot spinner's reduced-motion fallback slows the spin to 2s instead of stopping it
uncertain.wcag: 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA, honored as policy per ACCESSIBILITY.md)
uncertain.description: The pre-React boot screen spinner (.sr-boot-spin, an infinite 0.7s rotation) carries its own inline prefers-reduced-motion rule that merely slows the rotation to 2s per revolution rather than stopping it. This deliberately diverges from the published ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that 'loading spinners ... are reduced to near-instant.' In a production build the gap is neutralized: Vite injects the bundled globals.css as a render-blocking <link>, and its document-wide `* { animation-duration: 0.001ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important }` RM block (globals.css:588-594) overrides the inline rule at first paint (author !important beats normal declarations), freezing the spinner. The slow spin therefore only manifests in dev mode (JS-injected styles arrive after first paint) or if the bundled stylesheet fails to load. No WCAG AA failure: the boot screen has no parallel content and the spinner is a loading-phase progress indicator (2.2.2 exception), but it is the one motion source not strictly covered by the kill, and it makes the blanket 'near-instant' statement technically inaccurate for the pre-CSS window.
uncertain.fix: Either change the inline rule to `.sr-boot-spin { animation: none; }` (the frozen ring still communicates loading via the role="status" aria-label "Loading SnowRaven" on line 28), or — if the slow rotation is a deliberate 'gentle feedback' choice — note that one exception in ACCESSIBILITY.md's Reduced Motion section so the published claim stays exactly true.

uncertain.title: Four inline `animation: 'spin …'` styles in MapExplorer bypass the .spin class convention
uncertain.wcag: 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (policy per ACCESSIBILITY.md) — regression-risk only, no current failure
uncertain.description: MapExplorer.tsx applies the spinner keyframes via inline style objects instead of the shared `.spin` class at four sites: line 657 (map loading chip, 'spin 1s linear infinite'), line 682 ('Locating…' spinner, 'spin 0.7s linear infinite'), line 1003 and line 1224 (hotspots / media-targets 'Finding…' spinners, 'spin 1s linear infinite'). There is NO current user impact: the reduced-motion kill in globals.css:588-594 uses a universal `*` selector with `!important` longhands, and author !important declarations override inline styles, so these spinners are correctly frozen for reduced-motion users today. The risk is silent regression: these are the only animations in the codebase that escape the `.spin` class, so any future refactor that scopes the RM block to classes (e.g. `.spin { animation: none }`) instead of `*` would leave these four spinning for reduced-motion users with nothing failing visibly. Reported once; all four locations listed here.
uncertain.fix: Replace the inline `animation:` declarations with `className="spin"` at MapExplorer.tsx lines 657, 682, 1003, and 1224 (matching every other spinner in the app), so all spinner motion flows through the one class the reduced-motion CSS is built around.

uncertain.title: Statistics map rank-pin numerals are fixed 10px SVG text — only text in the app that ignores the Text Size control
uncertain.description: RankIcon renders a fixed 24×24 SVG with `fontSize="10"` for the rank numbers on the Statistics geographic map pins (BirdingStats.tsx:865, 871). The numeral does not scale with the Text Size control or OS text size. Mitigations: it is map content (markers on a map get latitude under 1.4.10/1.4.4), and the same ranking is available as scalable text in the "Top locations by checklists/species" lists directly below (BirdingStats.tsx:906, 921). Reported as polish, plus a note: the icon fills are hardcoded hex (`#2D8653`, `#3B82F6`, echoed in the legend swatches at BirdingStats.tsx:888/892 and the popup gray `#71717A` at :876), which violates the project's own --sr-* token rule.
uncertain.fix: Size the SVG in em (width/height '1.5em') so the pin and numeral track the root scale, or accept as map content and document it; swap the hardcoded hexes for var(--sr-*) tokens while there.

uncertain.title: Map Explorer filters accordion clamps to maxHeight 600px with overflow:hidden — fails closed if content ever exceeds it
uncertain.description: The collapsible filter panel animates via `maxHeight: filterOpen ? 600 : 0` with `overflow: 'hidden'`. Measuring the current contents (species select, date range, county, breeding seg-control, media select ≈300px at 100%; ≈450-500px at 200% with seg-control wrapping), there is headroom today, so this is not a present-day failure. But the construction fails silently: any future filter addition, or further text growth, pushes the bottom controls (the Media select) past 600px where they are clipped and unreachable with no scrollbar — the classic animated-max-height trap. Flagged so it isn't extended blindly.
uncertain.fix: Animate with `grid-template-rows: 0fr/1fr` + `min-height: 0` (no hard cap), or raise the open clamp to a generous `maxHeight: 'none'` after the transition ends, keeping 600px only as the transition target.

uncertain.title: Comparer media/side-header cells fixed at 132px
uncertain.description: The per-row media/count cell (`width: 132, flexShrink: 0`, ChecklistComparer.tsx:74) and its matching SideHeader (`width: 132`, :506) are fixed pixel widths holding 0.75rem text and badges. At 200% the cell contents (count + breeding-code badge + media badges) exceed 132px and push into the species-name column. Same family as the Statistics fixed-px finding but a separate file/owner, listed for completeness.
uncertain.fix: Use a rem width (e.g. '9rem') or `minWidth` so the cell grows with its text; keep header and cell sharing one constant.

uncertain.title: Mobile filter-panel focus trap snapshots focusables once at open — focus can escape after content inside the panel changes
uncertain.wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (published claim: 'keeps it there while open')
uncertain.description: The statement says opening the Map Explorer filter panel 'moves focus into the panel and keeps it there while open' — and the trap (MapExplorer.tsx:187-221) does focus the first element, wrap Tab/Shift+Tab, and return focus on Escape. However `focusable` is queried once when the panel opens; the wrap comparison uses the stale `first`/`last` references. The panel's content is dynamic (the Filters accordion expands, async hotspot/target fetches append in-view list rows after the snapshot's last element), so after such a change, Tab from the true last element no longer matches `last` and focus walks out of the overlay onto the map content behind the backdrop. Edge case, but it makes the 'keeps it there' claim conditionally false.
uncertain.fix: Re-query the focusable list inside the keydown handler (or on each Tab press) instead of capturing first/last at open time.
